quick_question.prompt: There is a CSV file shipments_2025.csv in this folder: the export of our 2025 shipments. Which carrier is the most reliable?
quick_question.answer:
**Falke Transport** is the most reliable carrier in the 2025 data. It has the highest on-time delivery rate, and its loss and damage rates are both low.

| Carrier | Shipments | On-time | Lost | Damaged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Falke Transport** | 2,020 | **91.3%** | 0.4% | 0.8% |
| Gams Cargo | 1,129 | 89.3% | 0.4% | 0.9% |
| Luchs Logistik | 1,237 | 88.6% | 0.2% | 1.3% |
| Biber Freight | 1,532 | 86.0% | 0.7% | 3.5% |

On-time means delivered on or before `promised_date`, measured over delivered shipments only.

Two things to know:

- **The file needed cleaning first.** It had 125 duplicate rows (exact copies with the same `shipment_id`), which I removed, leaving 5,918 shipments. "Biber Freight" also appeared under three spellings ("Biber Freight GmbH", "BIBER FREIGHT"), which I merged.
- **Luchs Logistik Express is a problem.** Only 42% of its 78 Express shipments arrived on time, while its Standard service was at 92%. If you're choosing a carrier for Express, avoid Luchs. Falke and Gams Cargo Express were both above 92%.

I didn't save the cleaning script to a file. I can add one if you want to rerun this on a new export.

check_first.prompt: There is a CSV file shipments_2025.csv in this folder: the export of our 2025 shipments. Before any analysis, check the table for data quality problems: repeated rows, different spellings of the same name, impossible or extreme values, and missing values. For each problem give the number of rows, one example and the evidence. Do not fix anything yet.
check_first.answer:
I checked `shipments_2025.csv` (6,043 data rows, 16 columns) and changed nothing. The file has four real problems: exact duplicate rows, three spellings of one carrier, a weight column that is probably in grams for 905 rows, and empty delivery dates that are expected. Line numbers below are file lines, with the header on line 1.

| # | Problem | Rows | Example | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Exact duplicate rows** | 125 extra copies (239 rows in total) | SH-25-00871, lines 879–881 (three identical copies) | All 16 columns match. 103 IDs appear twice and 11 appear three times. After removing them, 5,918 unique IDs remain, numbered 1–5918 with no gaps. No ID has conflicting content. |
| 2 | **Carrier name spelled three ways** | 570 rows (9.4%) | Line 903 "Biber Freight GmbH" (SH-25-00891); line 3061 "BIBER FREIGHT" (SH-25-03005) | "Biber Freight" 970 rows, "Biber Freight GmbH" 491, "BIBER FREIGHT" 79. The other five carriers each have one spelling. |
| 3 | **Impossible weights, probably grams in a kg column** | 905 rows (15%) with weight ≥ 1,000 kg | Line 4487, SH-25-04399: 480,000 kg for 32 parcels, €204.61. Line 4817, SH-25-04725: 50,700 kg for one parcel, €49.29 | Largest value 545,500 kg. Every one of the 905 values is a multiple of 100, against 0.1% of the other rows. Median weight per parcel is 12,500 kg, against 12.6 kg for the rest. Dividing by 1,000 makes weight fit cost: mean absolute error about €7 against about €5,800 unscaled. The unit is my inference, so confirm it with whoever exported the data. |
| 4 | **Empty delivery dates** | 71 rows | Line 657, SH-25-00653 (status "lost") | 44 are "in_transit" (shipped 19–31 Dec) and 27 are "lost". Every delivered row has a date, so these blanks are expected. They do depend on when the export was made. |

Items to note but not counted as errors:
- **Expensive Express shipment:** line 1989, SH-25-01953, costs €115.84 for 103 km, which is €1.12/km against a median of about €0.15/km for Express. It is extreme but not clearly wrong.
- **Promised dates in 2026:** 37 late-December shipments have promised dates up to 6 Jan 2026. This is correct, but it matters for year-end cut-offs.
- **Five round weights under 1,000 kg:** 600 kg and 900 kg. With the parcel counts they look plausible, so I left them alone.

Checks that found nothing: no empty cells other than delivery dates, no stray whitespace, no delivery before shipment, no promise before shipment, city and country always match, and each city has at most two distances (probably one per warehouse, which I did not verify). No shipments or deliveries fall on a weekend, which is worth knowing but is not a defect.

Once you confirm the weight unit, I can clean the file in a separate copy: drop the 125 duplicate rows, standardise the carrier name, and divide the affected weights by 1,000.
